<script>
  // Restore the saved color scheme preference, or
  // enact the browser preference if "automatic", 
  // without expecting DOM load to have completed.
  //
  // Also restore any saved readingmode and ToC display preferences.
  function initializeReadingPreferences() {
    let saved_theme = localStorage.getItem("ar5iv_theme") || "automatic";
    if (saved_theme === "automatic") {
      if (window.matchMedia("(prefers-color-scheme: dark)").matches) {
        saved_theme = "dark";
      }
    }
    if (saved_theme == "dark") {
      document.documentElement.setAttribute("data-theme", "dark");
    } else {
      document.documentElement.setAttribute("data-theme", "light");
    }

    const tocDisplay = localStorage.getItem('arxiv_html_paper_toc_display');
    if (tocDisplay) {
      document.documentElement.setAttribute("data-toc-display", tocDisplay);
    }
    const readingMode = localStorage.getItem('arxiv_html_paper_reading_mode');
    if (readingMode) {
      document.documentElement.setAttribute("data-reading-mode", readingMode);
    }
  }
  // Run as soon as JS starts, to minimize repainting
  initializeReadingPreferences();
</script>

  /* Reading mode hides the chrome and the empty .arxiv-html-header marker: the pinned JS reads
     the marker's display to know which way to toggle. The marker draws no box. */
  .arxiv-html-header { display: contents; }
  html[data-reading-mode="enabled"] :is(.arxiv-html-site-chrome, .arxiv-html-header, .ds-site-footer) { display: none; }
  /* The paper controls' icons are blocks, so they sit centred (the pinned JS shows the theme
     icon by making its span a block). */
  .arxiv-html-site-chrome .ds-site-header-tools svg { display: block; width: 18px; height: 18px; flex-shrink: 0; fill: currentColor; }
  /* ar5iv dims every image in dark mode and puts it on a white wash, for paper figures;
     arXiv's own render as they are (the logo on the bar, the funder logos on their white
     chips). Important: ar5iv's dark rules are unlayered, as specific as
     :root:not([data-theme]) img:not(.ltx_no_dark_filter). */
  :is(.ds-site-header, .ds-site-footer) img { filter: none !important; }
  .ds-site-header img { background-color: transparent !important; }

  /* Wide (the theme's 1280px): the theme lays the body out as a grid whose full-width top rows
     were the band's and its sticky reader bar's. The band takes the first and scrolls away; the
     header, the paper's bar (no site navigation, the paper's controls), takes the second and
     stays in view, the one sticky bar, with the anchor clearance that requires (DESIGN-POLICIES).
     The controls show their names. */
  @media (min-width: 1280px) {
    html { scroll-padding-top: 80px; }
    .arxiv-html-site-chrome { display: contents; }
    .arxiv-html-site-chrome > #ds-announcement { grid-area: announce; }
    .arxiv-html-site-chrome > .ds-site-header { grid-area: header; position: sticky; top: 0; z-index: 3; }
    .arxiv-html-site-chrome .tool-icon { display: none; }
  }
  /* Narrow: the header scrolls away, and the controls show icons (names kept for screen
     readers; Why HTML? goes). The theme's contents panel is fixed below where its old sticky
     bar was, and hidden only once the reader has closed it, so until then it is an invisible box
     over the header and the paper: it shows only while open, under the chrome, in its place in
     the page. The paper's footer (build logs, reporting instructions) keeps the text's side
     inset; the theme gives it none, so it met the screen edges. */
  @media (max-width: 1279px) {
    .arxiv-html-site-chrome .tool-wide { display: none; }
    .arxiv-html-site-chrome .tool-label { position: absolute; width: 1px; height: 1px; overflow: hidden; clip: rect(0 0 0 0); white-space: nowrap; }
    html:not([data-toc-display="block"]) .ltx_page_navbar { display: none; }
    .ltx_page_navbar { position: absolute; top: auto; }
    .arxiv-html-footer { padding-inline: 1rem; }
  }

<p id="p1.2" class="ltx_p">001</p>

<h1 class="ltx_title ltx_title_document">Unlimited OCR Works 2
<br class="ltx_break"><span id="id1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic" style="font-size:120%;">Pioneering the OCR-3.0 Era: From Long- to Unlimited-Horizon Parsing</span>
</h1>
<div class="ltx_authors">
<span class="ltx_creator ltx_role_author">
<span class="ltx_personname">Baidu ERNIE Team
</span></span></div>

<div id="abstract1" class="ltx_abstract"><h6 class="ltx_title ltx_title_abstract">Abstract</h6>
    
<p id="abstract1.1" class="ltx_p">Unlimited OCR ushers the era of long-horizon parsing, substantially mitigating the growth of working memory as document lengthens. However, as document length scales to hundreds of pages, the visual context grows substantially, sharply increasing the computational cost of each decoding step and limiting the scalability of ultra-long document parsing. Inspired by human book transcription via localized focus without re-scanning preceding pages, we introduce Unlimited OCR 2, a document parsing model that looks only at what it transcribes. Building on Unlimited OCR, we upgrade all the decoder attention modules to Sparse Reference Sliding Window Attention (SR-SWA), bounding active reference tokens to a fixed capacity and thus sustaining constant computational costs across arbitrarily long documents. By combining SR-SWA with Unlimited-Horizon Decoding Paradigm, Unlimited OCR 2 enables document parsing over virtually unlimited lengths without prohibitive memory overhead. At the hundred-page scale, Unlimited OCR 2 achieves 7.0<math id="abstract1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\times" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo>×</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\times</annotation></semantics></math> and 5.6<math id="abstract1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\times" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo>×</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\times</annotation></semantics></math> per-step speedups over Full Attention and R-SWA, respectively. Furthermore, it delivers state-of-the-art end-to-end performance on both MPDocBench and MarathonDocBench, our newly proposed benchmark targeting hundred-page document parsing. Ultimately, the capacity for uninterrupted, one-shot document parsing signifies a fundamental paradigm shift into the OCR 3.0 era.</p>
  
</div>
<figure id="S0.F1" class="ltx_figure"><img src="2610.39308v2/teaser.png" id="S0.F1.g1" class="ltx_graphics ltx_centering ltx_img_landscape" style="aspect-ratio:381/203;" width="381" height="203" alt="Refer to caption">
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure"><span id="S0.F1.3" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Figure 1</span>: </span><span id="S0.F1.4" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">R-SWA vs SR-SWA. R-SWA computes attention over all visual tokens across pages, inducing extreme visual redundancy; SR-SWA sparsely attends to relevant visual regions, aligning machine decoding with human reading intuition.</span></figcaption>
</figure>
<div class="ltx_pagination ltx_role_newpage"></div>

<section id="S1" class="ltx_section">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_section"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_section">1 </span>Introduction</h2>

<div id="S1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<blockquote id="S1.p1.1" class="ltx_quote">
<p id="S1.p1.1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S1.p1.1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">“Pixels are my body, and tokens are my blood. I have parsed over a thousand pages. Unknown to KV cache. Nor known to context limits. So, as I pray: Unlimited OCR Works.”</span></p><span class="ltx_rule" style="width:100%;height:1px;--ltx-bg-color:black;display:inline-block;"> </span>
<p id="S1.p1.1.2" class="ltx_p ltx_align_right"><span id="S1.p1.1.2.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:80%;">Snarcy on huggingface ( Adapted from <span id="S1.p1.1.2.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">UBW</span>)</span></p>
</blockquote>
</div>
<div id="S1.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S1.p2.1" class="ltx_p">Document parsing has undergone a major paradigm shift, transitioning from traditional multi-stage pipelines (OCR-1.0) <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib6" title="" class="ltx_ref">5</a>, <a href="#bib.bib27" title="" class="ltx_ref">40</a>, <a href="#bib.bib7" title="" class="ltx_ref">6</a>, <a href="#bib.bib9" title="" class="ltx_ref">22</a>, <a href="#bib.bib8" title="" class="ltx_ref">26</a>, <a href="#bib.bib26" title="" class="ltx_ref">20</a>, <a href="#bib.bib10" title="" class="ltx_ref">8</a>]</cite> with handcrafted detection and recognition modules to end-to-end Vision-Language Models (OCR-2.0) <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib15" title="" class="ltx_ref">19</a>, <a href="#bib.bib5" title="" class="ltx_ref">7</a>, <a href="#bib.bib41" title="" class="ltx_ref">21</a>, <a href="#bib.bib13" title="" class="ltx_ref">31</a>, <a href="#bib.bib20" title="" class="ltx_ref">18</a>]</cite>. By formulating document understanding as a unified sequence-to-sequence transcription task, OCR-2.0 frameworks effectively eliminate cumulative pipeline errors. Our previous work, Unlimited OCR <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib19" title="" class="ltx_ref">37</a>]</cite>, pushed OCR-2.0 boundaries to tens of pages by using Reference Sliding Window Attention (R-SWA) to maintain a constant KV cache. Nevertheless, it still computes attention over all visual tokens across pages during decoding. As document length scales, this persistent attention to non-informative visual tokens severely escalates visual redundancy, compounding the difficulty of end-to-end inference. This visual attention bottleneck naturally prompts a fundamental question: how can we transition from length-limited parsing to an unlimited one-shot paradigm and genuinely inaugurate the OCR-3.0 era?</p>
</div>
<div id="S1.p3" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S1.p3.1" class="ltx_p">To answer this question, human transcription of lengthy books provides a clear physical intuition for parsing scaling: as we copy text page by page, we maintain localized visual focus, casting only momentary glances back when cross-page references are needed, rather than keeping the entire volume active in mind. This cognitive mechanism reveals that visual dependencies in multi-page documents are inherently page-sparse yet intra-page concentrated. However, standard dense global attention completely overlooks this sparse dynamic, incurring redundant attention interactions across all pages. This not only incurs prohibitive computational overhead, but also leads to severe memory bottlenecks as document length scales. To break through these efficiency and memory bottlenecks, we align machine perception with human reading patterns and present Unlimited OCR 2, pioneering an unlimited-horizon parsing framework for the OCR-3.0 era. Our main contributions are as follows:</p>
<ul id="S1.I1" class="ltx_itemize">
<li id="S1.I1.i1" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="S1.I1.i1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S1.I1.i1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We introduce Sparse Reference Sliding Window Attention (SR-SWA), a hierarchical sparse attention mechanism designed for unlimited visual context. Specifically, Page Gate first narrows each query’s visual reference scope from the entire document to relevant pages while robustly modeling multi-page positional relationships. Token Sieve selectively incorporates top-<math id="S1.I1.i1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="k" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>k</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">k</annotation></semantics></math> remote token buckets to capture long-range visual dependencies, thereby drastically reducing attention overhead while preserving comprehensive context.</p>
</div></li>
<li id="S1.I1.i2" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="S1.I1.i2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S1.I1.i2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We introduce MarathonDocBench, a benchmark for hundred-page document parsing. It substantially extends existing evaluations in document length and cross-page structural complexity, enabling a comprehensive assessment of long-document parsing performance in the hundred-page regime.</p>
</div></li>
<li id="S1.I1.i3" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="S1.I1.i3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S1.I1.i3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Comprehensive evaluations in long-horizon settings demonstrate that our approach maintains constant per-step decoding latency regardless of document length while achieving state-of-the-art end-to-end performance on multi-page benchmarks. Building on these advances, we establish an efficient unlimited-horizon parsing paradigm by integrating SR-SWA with the Unlimited-Horizon Decoding Paradigm, enabling document parsing over virtually unlimited lengths.</p>
</div></li>
</ul>
</div>
<div id="S1.p4" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S1.p4.1" class="ltx_p">In summary, SR-SWA fundamentally breaks the computational and memory bottlenecks of ultra-long visual context. Operating at constant per-step decoding latency with length-invariant accuracy across hundreds of pages, Unlimited OCR 2 unlocks scalable long-document parsing and paves the way for the OCR-3.0 era of unlimited-horizon understanding.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S2" class="ltx_section">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_section"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_section">2 </span>Related Works</h2>

<section id="S2.SS1" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">2.1 </span>VLM-based Document Parsing</h3>

<div id="S2.SS1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S2.SS1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Document parsing has increasingly been reshaped by advances in vision-language models, evolving from pipeline-based OCR-1.0 systems <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib6" title="" class="ltx_ref">5</a>, <a href="#bib.bib27" title="" class="ltx_ref">40</a>, <a href="#bib.bib7" title="" class="ltx_ref">6</a>, <a href="#bib.bib9" title="" class="ltx_ref">22</a>, <a href="#bib.bib8" title="" class="ltx_ref">26</a>, <a href="#bib.bib26" title="" class="ltx_ref">20</a>, <a href="#bib.bib10" title="" class="ltx_ref">8</a>]</cite>, which combine specialized page analysis modules with VLM-based decoding, to unified VLM-based OCR-2.0 systems that directly generate structured representations from document images. OCR-2.0 encompasses both single-page parsers <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib15" title="" class="ltx_ref">19</a>, <a href="#bib.bib5" title="" class="ltx_ref">7</a>, <a href="#bib.bib28" title="" class="ltx_ref">30</a>, <a href="#bib.bib41" title="" class="ltx_ref">21</a>, <a href="#bib.bib13" title="" class="ltx_ref">31</a>, <a href="#bib.bib20" title="" class="ltx_ref">18</a>]</cite> and Unlimited OCR <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib19" title="" class="ltx_ref">37</a>]</cite>, which extends end-to-end parsing to multi-page documents by jointly modeling their visual content within a shared context. However, although Unlimited OCR improves long-document efficiency with R-SWA, it still densely attends to all remote visual tokens, causing the visual context accessible to each decoding query to expand with document length and creating a fundamental scalability bottleneck at the hundred-page scale. Unlimited OCR 2 overcomes this limitation by explicitly bounding remote visual access, enabling attention-efficient end-to-end parsing of hundred-page documents and advancing document parsing into the OCR-3.0 era.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S2.SS2" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">2.2 </span>Efficient Long-Context Modeling</h3>

<div id="S2.SS2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S2.SS2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Efficient long-context modeling has been explored through both attention replacement and sparse attention. Linear or recurrent alternatives <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib29" title="" class="ltx_ref">11</a>, <a href="#bib.bib32" title="" class="ltx_ref">35</a>, <a href="#bib.bib30" title="" class="ltx_ref">15</a>, <a href="#bib.bib31" title="" class="ltx_ref">36</a>, <a href="#bib.bib33" title="" class="ltx_ref">17</a>]</cite> reduce long-context cost by summarizing historical information into compact states. Document parsing, however, requires long-range memory to preserve fine-grained visual evidence for accurate recognition and cross-page retrieval, which may not be fully retained within such compact representations.</p>
</div>
<div id="S2.SS2.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S2.SS2.p2.1" class="ltx_p">Sparse attention retains direct access to selected historical tokens or KV blocks while avoiding dense all-to-all computation. Early methods use predefined patterns such as local windows and global tokens <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib34" title="" class="ltx_ref">2</a>, <a href="#bib.bib35" title="" class="ltx_ref">39</a>]</cite>, whereas recent approaches adopt query-dependent retrieval. Hard-selection methods, such as Compressed Sparse Attention(CSA) <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib37" title="" class="ltx_ref">33</a>]</cite> and MiniMax Sparse Attention(MSA) <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib2" title="" class="ltx_ref">16</a>]</cite>, rely on discrete top-<math id="S2.SS2.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="k" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>k</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">k</annotation></semantics></math> routing and typically require auxiliary supervision or warmup. In contrast, DashAttention <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib3" title="" class="ltx_ref">13</a>]</cite> and HiLS <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib36" title="" class="ltx_ref">12</a>]</cite> incorporate differentiable or forward-integrated routing scores, enabling more direct end-to-end optimization.</p>
</div>
</section>
</section>
<section id="S3" class="ltx_section">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_section"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_section">3 </span>Methodology</h2>

<section id="S3.SS1" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">3.1 </span>Problem Setup</h3>

<section id="S3.SS1.SSS1" class="ltx_subsubsection">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsubsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsubsection">3.1.1 </span>Unlimited-horizon Parsing</h4>

<div id="S3.SS1.SSS1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.SS1.SSS1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Unlimited-horizon parsing aims to enable end-to-end processing of documents of arbitrary lengths, from single-page forms to massive multi-page documents, with bounded computational and memory complexities.
Formally, multi-page document parsing generates a transcription <math id="S3.SS1.SSS1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{Y}=(y_{1},\ldots,y_{L})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒴</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>y</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">…</mi><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>y</mi><mi>L</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{Y}=(y_{1},\ldots,y_{L})</annotation></semantics></math> from an ordered document <math id="S3.SS1.SSS1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{D}=(P_{1},\ldots,P_{N})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒟</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>P</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">…</mi><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>P</mi><mi>N</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{D}=(P_{1},\ldots,P_{N})</annotation></semantics></math> with visual tokens <math id="S3.SS1.SSS1.p1.m3" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="\mathcal{V}_{1:N}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒱</mi><msub><mrow></mrow><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo lspace="0.278em" rspace="0.278em">:</mo><mi>N</mi></mrow></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{V}_{1:N}</annotation></semantics></math>. At decoding step <math id="S3.SS1.SSS1.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="t" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>t</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t</annotation></semantics></math>, the model operates on:</p>
<table id="S3.E1" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S3.E1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{X}_{t}=\operatorname{Concat}\left(\mathcal{V}_{1},\ldots,\mathcal{V}_{N},y_{&lt;t}\right)." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒳</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>Concat</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo>(</mo><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒱</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">…</mi><mo>,</mo><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒱</mi><mi>N</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>y</mi><mrow><mphantom></mphantom><mo>&lt;</mo><mi>t</mi></mrow></msub><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{X}_{t}=\operatorname{Concat}\left(\mathcal{V}_{1},\ldots,\mathcal{V}_{N},y_{&lt;t}\right).</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(1)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S3.SS1.SSS1.p1.2" class="ltx_p">While Unlimited OCR constrained text history to a fixed sliding window via R-SWA, it still requires attending over all preceding visual tokens <math id="S3.SS1.SSS1.p1.m5" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="\mathcal{V}_{1:N}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒱</mi><msub><mrow></mrow><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo lspace="0.278em" rspace="0.278em">:</mo><mi>N</mi></mrow></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{V}_{1:N}</annotation></semantics></math>. In the hundred-page regime, this page-dependent visual expansion becomes the primary bottleneck. Decoupling visual context from page count <math id="S3.SS1.SSS1.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="N" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>N</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">N</annotation></semantics></math> to maintain a bounded computational and memory footprint directly motivates our proposed Sparse Reference Sliding Window Attention (SR-SWA).</p>
</div>
<figure id="S3.F2" class="ltx_figure"><object type="image/svg+xml" data="2610.39308v2/bench_compare.svg" id="S3.F2.g1" class="ltx_graphics ltx_centering ltx_img_landscape" style="aspect-ratio:476/160;" width="476" height="160"></object>
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure"><span id="S3.F2.3" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Figure 2</span>: </span><span id="S3.F2.4" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">MarathonDocBench versus MPDocBench. MarathonDocBench extends document length from tens to hundreds of pages (a), with substantially richer cross-page structures as shown in (b) and (c).</span></figcaption>
</figure>
</section>
<section id="S3.SS1.SSS2" class="ltx_subsubsection">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsubsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsubsection">3.1.2 </span>MarathonDocBench</h4>

<div id="S3.SS1.SSS2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.SS1.SSS2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Existing multi-page document parsing benchmarks neither extend to the hundred-page scale nor sufficiently capture the rich cross-page structures that emerge in long documents. To address this gap, we introduce MarathonDocBench, the first benchmark specifically designed for hundred-page document parsing. It contains 100 documents spanning 103–300 pages with 205k annotated layout elements, extending the document-length range by roughly an order of magnitude beyond MPDocBench <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib1" title="" class="ltx_ref">41</a>]</cite>.</p>
</div>
<div id="S3.SS1.SSS2.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.SS1.SSS2.p2.1" class="ltx_p">Beyond document length, MarathonDocBench contains substantially richer cross-page structures than MPDocBench, with cross-page text and tables appearing much more frequently and densely across documents, as summarized in Figure <a href="#S3.F2" title="Figure 2 ‣ 3.1.1 Unlimited-horizon Parsing ‣ 3.1 Problem Setup ‣ 3 Methodology ‣ Unlimited OCR Works 2Pioneering the OCR-3.0 Era: From Long- to Unlimited-Horizon Parsing" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">2</span></a>. This makes MarathonDocBench a substantially more challenging testbed for evaluating whether end-to-end parsers can preserve document-level structure while scaling from tens to hundreds of pages. To ensure reliable evaluation, structural annotations, including bounding boxes, block type, hierarchy, reading order, and cross-page continuations of text and tables, are initialized from a strong page-by-page parser and carefully refined by human annotators. Content transcriptions are initialized from the same parser outputs and verified through an iterative VLM-based refinement pipeline, with flagged disagreements adjudicated by human annotators.</p>
</div>
</section>
</section>
<section id="S3.SS2" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">3.2 </span>Architecture</h3>

<figure id="S3.F3" class="ltx_figure"><img src="2610.39308v2/method_4.png" id="S3.F3.g1" class="ltx_graphics ltx_centering ltx_img_landscape" style="aspect-ratio:476/196;" width="476" height="196" alt="Refer to caption">
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure"><span id="S3.F3.3" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Figure 3</span>: </span><span id="S3.F3.4" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Inspired by the process of humans copying books, we propose Unlimited OCR 2. SR-SWA combines Page Gate and Token Sieve to construct a fixed-length set of working reference visual tokens, substantially reducing computational and memory overhead while keeping both independent of document length throughout generation.</span></figcaption>
</figure>
<div id="S3.SS2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.SS2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Unlimited OCR 2 inherits the fundamental backbone from Unlimited OCR, leveraging DeepSeek OCR <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib11" title="" class="ltx_ref">28</a>]</cite> as its foundation. Specifically, it employs the DeepEncoder paired with a Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) decoder architecture featuring 3B total parameters and 500M activated parameters per token. Building upon this base, we replace the baseline R-SWA with our proposed SR-SWA as shown in Figure <a href="#S3.F3" title="Figure 3 ‣ 3.2 Architecture ‣ 3 Methodology ‣ Unlimited OCR Works 2Pioneering the OCR-3.0 Era: From Long- to Unlimited-Horizon Parsing" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">3</span></a>. While R-SWA bounds local interactions, its visual context scope still expands with growing document length, leading to noticeable latency accumulation over ultra-long horizons. By introducing a selective remote visual routing mechanism, SR-SWA strictly bounds the active context scope, enabling Unlimited OCR 2 to maintain a constant KV cache footprint across both text and visual modalities during unlimited-horizon decoding. We detail the inner mechanics of SR-SWA in the following subsections.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S3.SS3" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">3.3 </span>Sparse Reference Sliding Window Attention</h3>

<div id="S3.SS3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.SS3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Following standard block-sparse attention <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib2" title="" class="ltx_ref">16</a>, <a href="#bib.bib3" title="" class="ltx_ref">13</a>, <a href="#bib.bib37" title="" class="ltx_ref">33</a>, <a href="#bib.bib38" title="" class="ltx_ref">32</a>]</cite>,
we partition <math id="S3.SS3.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{X}_{t}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒳</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{X}_{t}</annotation></semantics></math> into fixed-size blocks <math id="S3.SS3.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\{\mathcal{B}_{b}\}_{b=1}^{B}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msubsup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℬ</mi><mi>b</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow><mrow><mi>b</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mi>B</mi></msubsup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\{\mathcal{B}_{b}\}_{b=1}^{B}</annotation></semantics></math>
and preserve a fixed local window <math id="S3.SS3.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{L}(q)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℒ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>q</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{L}(q)</annotation></semantics></math> for each query <math id="S3.SS3.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="q" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>q</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">q</annotation></semantics></math>.
SR-SWA constructs <math id="S3.SS3.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{S}(q)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒮</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>q</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{S}(q)</annotation></semantics></math> hierarchically,
using Page Gate for page-level organization and Token Sieve for fixed-budget selection.</p>
</div>
<section id="S3.SS3.SSS1" class="ltx_subsubsection">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsubsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsubsection">3.3.1 </span>Page Gate</h4>

<div id="S3.SS3.SSS1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.SS3.SSS1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">To eliminate irrelevant visual tokens and concentrate focus on the current page, Page Gate restricts the visual attention scope for a query <math id="S3.SS3.SSS1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="q" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>q</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">q</annotation></semantics></math> associated with page <math id="S3.SS3.SSS1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="g(q)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>g</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>q</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">g(q)</annotation></semantics></math> by retaining only blocks from designated target pages:</p>
<table id="S3.E2" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S3.E2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{C}_{\mathrm{page}}(q)=\left\{b\;\middle|\;\mathcal{B}_{b}\cap\mathcal{V}_{g(q)}\neq\emptyset\right\}." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒞</mi><mi>page</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>q</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo>{</mo><mi>b</mi><mo stretchy="true">|</mo><mrow><mrow><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℬ</mi><mi>b</mi></msub><mo>∩</mo><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒱</mi><mrow><mi>g</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>q</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></msub></mrow><mo>≠</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">∅</mi></mrow><mo>}</mo></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{C}_{\mathrm{page}}(q)=\left\{b\;\middle|\;\mathcal{B}_{b}\cap\mathcal{V}_{g(q)}\neq\emptyset\right\}.</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(2)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S3.SS3.SSS1.p1.2" class="ltx_p">Since block boundaries are independent of page boundaries, a candidate block may straddle adjacent pages. Meanwhile, to prevent positional explosion as page count scales, Page Gate factorizes each token position into a bounded page-level coordinate (following an alternating <math id="S3.SS3.SSS1.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0</annotation></semantics></math>–<math id="S3.SS3.SSS1.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>1</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1</annotation></semantics></math> pattern) and a monotonic intra-page coordinate:</p>
<table id="S3.E3" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S3.E3.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathbf{p}_{i,j}=\left[\mathbf{p}^{\mathrm{page}}_{i},\;\mathbf{p}^{\mathrm{intra}}_{i,j}\right]," display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>𝐩</mi><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>j</mi></mrow></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo>[</mo><mrow><msubsup><mi>𝐩</mi><mi>i</mi><mi>page</mi></msubsup><mo rspace="0.447em">,</mo><msubsup><mi>𝐩</mi><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>j</mi></mrow><mi>intra</mi></msubsup></mrow><mo>]</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathbf{p}_{i,j}=\left[\mathbf{p}^{\mathrm{page}}_{i},\;\mathbf{p}^{\mathrm{intra}}_{i,j}\right],</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(3)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S3.SS3.SSS1.p1.3" class="ltx_p">ensuring both stable length extrapolation and efficient cross-page visual routing.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S3.SS3.SSS2" class="ltx_subsubsection">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsubsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsubsection">3.3.2 </span>Token Sieve</h4>

<div id="S3.SS3.SSS2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.SS3.SSS2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">While Page Gate restricts the routing space across pages, efficient fixed-budget routing requires a principled block selection strategy. Conventional sparse routers typically rely on dense-attention distillation, which lacks direct alignment with the language modeling objective. Inspired by recent end-to-end routing designs <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib3" title="" class="ltx_ref">13</a>, <a href="#bib.bib36" title="" class="ltx_ref">12</a>]</cite>, Token Sieve directly optimizes fixed-budget block selection under the language modeling objective.</p>
</div>
<div id="S3.SS3.SSS2.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.SS3.SSS2.p2.1" class="ltx_p">Given the candidate set <math id="S3.SS3.SSS2.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{C}_{\mathrm{page}}(q)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒞</mi><mi>page</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>q</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{C}_{\mathrm{page}}(q)</annotation></semantics></math> from Page Gate, Token Sieve summarizes each candidate block <math id="S3.SS3.SSS2.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="b" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>b</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">b</annotation></semantics></math> into a compact key representation <math id="S3.SS3.SSS2.p2.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\bar{\mathbf{k}}_{b}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>𝐤</mi><mo>¯</mo></mover><mi>b</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\bar{\mathbf{k}}_{b}</annotation></semantics></math> and computes its relevance to query <math id="S3.SS3.SSS2.p2.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="q" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>q</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">q</annotation></semantics></math>. The router then forms a sparse routing distribution and retains only the top-<math id="S3.SS3.SSS2.p2.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="k" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>k</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">k</annotation></semantics></math> blocks:</p>
<table id="S3.E4" class="ltx_equationgroup ltx_eqn_table">
<tbody>
<tr id="S3.E4X" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_td ltx_align_right ltx_eqn_cell"><math id="S3.E4X.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\displaystyle s_{b}(q)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>s</mi><mi>b</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>q</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\displaystyle s_{b}(q)</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_td ltx_align_left ltx_eqn_cell"><math id="S3.E4X.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\displaystyle=\frac{\tilde{\mathbf{q}}^{\top}\bar{\mathbf{k}}_{b}}{\sqrt{d}},\qquad\boldsymbol{\pi}(q)=\alpha\text{-entmax}\left(\{s_{b}(q)\}_{b\in\mathcal{C}_{\mathrm{page}}(q)}\right)," display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo>=</mo><mstyle displaystyle="true"><mfrac><mrow><msup><mover accent="true"><mi>𝐪</mi><mo>~</mo></mover><mo>⊤</mo></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>𝐤</mi><mo>¯</mo></mover><mi>b</mi></msub></mrow><msqrt><mi>d</mi></msqrt></mfrac></mstyle><mo rspace="2.167em">,</mo><mi>𝝅</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>q</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mi>α</mi><mtext>-entmax</mtext><mo>(</mo><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><mi>s</mi><msub><mrow></mrow><mi>b</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>q</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo stretchy="false">}</mo><msub><mrow></mrow><mrow><mi>b</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒞</mi><mi>page</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>q</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></msub><mo>)</mo><mo>,</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\displaystyle=\frac{\tilde{\mathbf{q}}^{\top}\bar{\mathbf{k}}_{b}}{\sqrt{d}},\qquad\boldsymbol{\pi}(q)=\alpha\text{-entmax}\left(\{s_{b}(q)\}_{b\in\mathcal{C}_{\mathrm{page}}(q)}\right),</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="2" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equationgroup ltx_align_right">(4)</span></td></tr>
<tr id="S3.E4Xa" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_td ltx_align_right ltx_eqn_cell"><math id="S3.E4Xa.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\displaystyle\mathcal{S}(q)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒮</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>q</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\displaystyle\mathcal{S}(q)</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_td ltx_align_left ltx_eqn_cell"><math id="S3.E4Xa.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\displaystyle=\operatorname{TopK}\big(\boldsymbol{\pi}(q),k\big)." display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mphantom></mphantom><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>TopK</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo maxsize="1.200em" minsize="1.200em">(</mo><mrow><mi>𝝅</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>q</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo><mi>k</mi><mo maxsize="1.200em" minsize="1.200em">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\displaystyle=\operatorname{TopK}\big(\boldsymbol{\pi}(q),k\big).</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S3.SS3.SSS2.p2.2" class="ltx_p">Here, <math id="S3.SS3.SSS2.p2.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="d" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>d</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">d</annotation></semantics></math> denotes the hidden dimension. By selectively attending to a fixed number of top-<math id="S3.SS3.SSS2.p2.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="k" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>k</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">k</annotation></semantics></math> remote buckets, Token Sieve captures long-range visual dependencies with minimal computational overhead. To preserve relative preferences among selected blocks, the routing probabilities are converted into a mean-centered log-prior:</p>
<table id="S3.E5" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S3.E5.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\beta_{b}(q)=\log\pi_{b}(q)-\frac{1}{|\mathcal{S}(q)|}\sum_{b^{\prime}\in\mathcal{S}(q)}\log\pi_{b^{\prime}}(q),\qquad b\in\mathcal{S}(q)." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>β</mi><mi>b</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>q</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mrow><mrow><mi>log</mi><mo lspace="0.167em">⁡</mo><msub><mi>π</mi><mi>b</mi></msub></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>q</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>−</mo><mrow><mfrac><mn>1</mn><mrow><mo stretchy="false">|</mo><mrow><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒮</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>q</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">|</mo></mrow></mfrac><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><munder><mo movablelimits="false">∑</mo><mrow><msup><mi>b</mi><mo>′</mo></msup><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒮</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>q</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></munder><mrow><mrow><mi>log</mi><mo lspace="0.167em">⁡</mo><msub><mi>π</mi><msup><mi>b</mi><mo>′</mo></msup></msub></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>q</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo rspace="2.167em">,</mo><mrow><mi>b</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒮</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>q</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\beta_{b}(q)=\log\pi_{b}(q)-\frac{1}{|\mathcal{S}(q)|}\sum_{b^{\prime}\in\mathcal{S}(q)}\log\pi_{b^{\prime}}(q),\qquad b\in\mathcal{S}(q).</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(5)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
</div>
<div id="S3.SS3.SSS2.p3" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.SS3.SSS2.p3.1" class="ltx_p">With the selected remote blocks <math id="S3.SS3.SSS2.p3.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{S}(q)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒮</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>q</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{S}(q)</annotation></semantics></math> and the fixed local window <math id="S3.SS3.SSS2.p3.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{L}(q)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℒ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>q</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{L}(q)</annotation></semantics></math>, each query attends to a length-agnostic retained token set defined as:</p>
<table id="S3.E6" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S3.E6.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{R}(q)=\mathcal{L}(q)\cup\bigcup_{b\in\mathcal{S}(q)}\mathcal{B}_{b}.\vskip-5.69046pt" display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℛ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>q</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mrow><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℒ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>q</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo rspace="0.055em">∪</mo><mrow><munder><mo movablelimits="false">⋃</mo><mrow><mi>b</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒮</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>q</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></munder><msub><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℬ</mi><mi>b</mi></msub></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{R}(q)=\mathcal{L}(q)\cup\bigcup_{b\in\mathcal{S}(q)}\mathcal{B}_{b}.\vskip-5.69046pt</annotation></semantics></math></td>

<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(6)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S3.SS3.SSS2.p3.2" class="ltx_p">The attention weights over <math id="S3.SS3.SSS2.p3.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{R}(q)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℛ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>q</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{R}(q)</annotation></semantics></math> are computed as:</p>
<table id="S3.E7" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S3.E7.m1" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="\alpha_{j}(q)=\operatorname{Softmax}\left(\frac{q^{\top}k_{j}}{\sqrt{d}}+\mathbb{I}\!\left[b(j)\in\mathcal{S}(q)\right]\beta_{b(j)}(q)\right)," display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>α</mi><mi>j</mi></msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>q</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>=</mo><mi>Softmax</mi><mrow><mo>(</mo><mfrac><mrow><msup><mi>q</mi><mo>⊤</mo></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>k</mi><mi>j</mi></msub></mrow><msqrt><mi>d</mi></msqrt></mfrac><mo>+</mo><mpadded style="width:0.219em;" width="0.219em"><mi>𝕀</mi></mpadded><mrow><mo>[</mo><mi>b</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>j</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>∈</mo><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒮</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>q</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>]</mo></mrow><msub><mi>β</mi><mrow><mi>b</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>j</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>q</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>,</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\alpha_{j}(q)=\operatorname{Softmax}\left(\frac{q^{\top}k_{j}}{\sqrt{d}}+\mathbb{I}\!\left[b(j)\in\mathcal{S}(q)\right]\beta_{b(j)}(q)\right),</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(7)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S3.SS3.SSS2.p3.3" class="ltx_p">where the softmax is normalized over all tokens in <math id="S3.SS3.SSS2.p3.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{R}(q)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℛ</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>q</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{R}(q)</annotation></semantics></math>, <math id="S3.SS3.SSS2.p3.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="b(j)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>b</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>j</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">b(j)</annotation></semantics></math> denotes the block containing token <math id="S3.SS3.SSS2.p3.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="j" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>j</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">j</annotation></semantics></math>, and <math id="S3.SS3.SSS2.p3.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="k_{j}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>k</mi><mi>j</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">k_{j}</annotation></semantics></math> denotes its key projection. Tokens within the local window use standard attention logits, while tokens from selected remote blocks additionally incorporate the corresponding routing bias. Since the routing bias directly participates in these logits, gradients from the parsing objective can propagate to the routing module, enabling end-to-end optimization without an auxiliary KL-divergence distillation loss.</p>
</div>

</div>
<div id="alg1.l7" class="ltx_listingline">
                <span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_listingline"><span id="alg1.l7.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:80%;">7:</span></span>
                
                
              <math id="alg1.l7.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="y_{1}\leftarrow\textsc{Decode}(\mathcal{C})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>y</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo stretchy="false">←</mo><mrow><mtext class="ltx_font_smallcaps">Decode</mtext><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒞</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">y_{1}\leftarrow\textsc{Decode}(\mathcal{C})</annotation></semantics></math>; <math id="alg1.l7.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="Y\leftarrow y_{1}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>Y</mi><mo stretchy="false">←</mo><msub><mi>y</mi><mn>1</mn></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">Y\leftarrow y_{1}</annotation></semantics></math>

<div id="alg1.l8" class="ltx_listingline">

              <span id="alg1.l8.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">for</span> <math id="alg1.l8.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="k=2" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">k=2</annotation></semantics></math> <span id="alg1.l8.4" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">to</span> <math id="alg1.l8.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="K" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>K</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">K</annotation></semantics></math> <span id="alg1.l8.5" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">do</span>

              <span id="alg1.l12.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">return</span> <math id="alg1.l12.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="Y" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>Y</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">Y</annotation></semantics></math>

</figure>
<figure id="S3.F4" class="ltx_figure"><img src="2610.39308v2/prefill_overlap_editable.png" id="S3.F4.g1" class="ltx_graphics ltx_centering ltx_img_landscape" style="aspect-ratio:476/192;" width="476" height="192" alt="Refer to caption">
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure"><span id="S3.F4.3" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Figure 4</span>: </span><span id="S3.F4.4" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Comparison of (a) standard decoding and (b) our Unlimited-Horizon Decoding paradigm. Standard decoding retains visual KV caches for all pages, causing GPU memory usage to grow linearly with document length and eventually overflow. Our paradigm divides long documents into manageable chunks and processes them sequentially, reusing the KV cache of shared boundary pages and releasing inactive caches to keep GPU memory usage bounded while preserving cross-chunk continuity.</span></figcaption>
</figure>
</section>
</section>
<section id="S3.SS4" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">3.4 </span>Unlimited-Horizon Decoding Paradigm</h3>

<div id="S3.SS4.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.SS4.p1.1" class="ltx_p">While SR-SWA bounds the number of reference tokens accessed by each query, processing extremely long multi-page documents remains constrained by the GPU memory required to prefill and retain their visual KV caches. As illustrated in Figure <a href="#S3.F4" title="Figure 4 ‣ 3.3.2 Token Sieve ‣ 3.3 Sparse Reference Sliding Window Attention ‣ 3 Methodology ‣ Unlimited OCR Works 2Pioneering the OCR-3.0 Era: From Long- to Unlimited-Horizon Parsing" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">4</span></a>, conventional all-at-once prefill keeps all page-level visual KV caches in memory, causing the memory footprint to grow linearly with document length. To overcome this limitation, we introduce the Unlimited-Horizon Decoding Paradigm, which partitions the document into overlapping page-level chunks and processes them sequentially. Adjacent chunks share their boundary page, whose KV cache is directly reused to preserve cross-chunk continuity, while visual KV caches outside the active chunk are released. Consequently, only a fixed-size chunk remains resident in GPU memory, bounding the memory footprint independently of the total document length. The complete procedure is formally described in Algorithm <a href="#alg1" title="Algorithm 1 ‣ 3.3.2 Token Sieve ‣ 3.3 Sparse Reference Sliding Window Attention ‣ 3 Methodology ‣ Unlimited OCR Works 2Pioneering the OCR-3.0 Era: From Long- to Unlimited-Horizon Parsing" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">1</span></a>.</p>
</div>
</section>
</section>
<section id="S4" class="ltx_section">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_section"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_section">4 </span>Experimental Settings</h2>

<section id="S4.SS1" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">4.1 </span>Data Engine</h3>

<div id="S4.SS1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">To train Unlimited OCR 2 for versatile document parsing, we construct a large-scale multimodal corpus comprising <math id="S4.SS1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="2\text{M}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mtext>M</mtext></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2\text{M}</annotation></semantics></math> multi-page and <math id="S4.SS1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="10\text{M}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>10</mn><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mtext>M</mtext></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">10\text{M}</annotation></semantics></math> single-page documents. Pseudo-labels across both single- and multi-page subsets are extracted from MinerU2.5-Pro <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib8" title="" class="ltx_ref">26</a>]</cite> and PaddleOCR-VL-v1.6 <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib27" title="" class="ltx_ref">40</a>]</cite>, tailored to their respective domain strengths. To enrich visual and layout diversity, we additionally incorporate versatile synthetic document generation pipelines. Across both real and synthetic data, we leverage VLM-based multi-dimensional feature analysis to conduct balance filtering, ensuring uniform coverage over complex layout distributions. Finally, to explicitly fortify structural hierarchy and cross-page continuity in multi-page scenarios, we apply MinerU-Popo <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib4" title="" class="ltx_ref">34</a>]</cite> refinement alongside dedicated heuristic post-processing rules to reconcile layout inconsistencies across adjacent page boundaries.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S4.SS2" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">4.2 </span>Implementation Details</h3>

<div id="S4.SS2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We initialize Unlimited OCR 2 from the Unlimited OCR checkpoint and perform post-training for 1 epoch on the curated dataset. Training is conducted on a cluster of <math id="S4.SS2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="25\times 8" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>25</mn><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><mn>8</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">25\times 8</annotation></semantics></math> GPU NVIDIA H800 nodes with a global batch size of 1,600 and a maximum sequence length of 64K tokens. During training, we freeze both the DeepEncoder and the aligner, optimizing only the LLM parameters. Optimization is carried out using the AdamW optimizer with a cosine learning rate decay schedule, starting at an initial learning rate of <math id="S4.SS2.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="2.5\times 10^{-4}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>2.5</mn><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><msup><mn>10</mn><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>4</mn></mrow></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2.5\times 10^{-4}</annotation></semantics></math>. The entire training workflow is implemented using the MS-Swift framework. For deployment, the Unlimited-Horizon Decoding Paradigm is integrated into SGLang to facilitate efficient long-document inference.</p>
</div>
</section>
</section>
<section id="S5" class="ltx_section">

</span></div>
</figure>
<div id="S5.SS1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S5.SS1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">To comprehensively evaluate Unlimited OCR 2 on document parsing across varying lengths, we conduct experiments on two challenging multi-page benchmarks: MPDocBench <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib1" title="" class="ltx_ref">41</a>]</cite> (up to 30 pages) and our proposed MarathonDocBench (ranging from 100 to 300 pages). Following the official evaluation protocol of MPDocBench, we report Edit Distance for textual content and reading order recognition, TEDS for table structure recognition, CDM for mathematical formula recognition, and F1 score for figure region detection. To further evaluate cross-page consistency, we include T-TextEdit and T-TEDS to assess text and table parsing across page boundaries, respectively. An overall score aggregated across these fine-grained structural categories is also computed to summarize overall parsing performance.</p>
</div>

<td id="S5.T3.7.12.6" class="ltx_td ltx_nopad_l ltx_nopad_r ltx_align_center ltx_border_bb" style="padding-left:1.6pt;padding-right:1.6pt;"><span id="S5.T3.7.12.6.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:80%;">89.60</span></td>
<td id="S5.T3.7.12.7" class="ltx_td ltx_nopad_l ltx_nopad_r ltx_align_center ltx_border_bb" style="padding-left:1.6pt;padding-right:1.6pt;"><span id="S5.T3.7.12.7.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:80%;">92.70</span></td>
<td id="S5.T3.7.12.8" class="ltx_td ltx_nopad_l ltx_nopad_r ltx_align_center ltx_border_bb" style="padding-left:1.6pt;padding-right:1.6pt;"><span id="S5.T3.7.12.8.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:80%;">0.128</span></td></tr>
</table>
</figure>
</section>
<section id="S5.SS2" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">5.2 </span>Main Results</h3>

<div id="S5.SS2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S5.SS2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">As visually summarized in Figure <a href="#S5.F6" title="Figure 6 ‣ 5.3.1 Feasibility of Unlimited-horizon Parsing ‣ 5.3 Scaling with Document Length ‣ 5 Evaluation ‣ Unlimited OCR Works 2Pioneering the OCR-3.0 Era: From Long- to Unlimited-Horizon Parsing" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">6</span></a> and further detailed in Table <a href="#S5.T1" title="Table 1 ‣ 5.1 Benchmarks and Metrics ‣ 5 Evaluation ‣ Unlimited OCR Works 2Pioneering the OCR-3.0 Era: From Long- to Unlimited-Horizon Parsing" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">1</span></a> and Table <a href="#S5.T2" title="Table 2 ‣ 5.1 Benchmarks and Metrics ‣ 5 Evaluation ‣ Unlimited OCR Works 2Pioneering the OCR-3.0 Era: From Long- to Unlimited-Horizon Parsing" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">2</span></a>, Unlimited OCR 2 takes a significant step toward the OCR 3.0 era, advancing document parsing along three key dimensions. First, it establishes the practical feasibility of hundred-page end-to-end parsing, achieving a score of 77.06 on MarathonDocBench and demonstrating its ability to handle documents at a scale beyond conventional multi-page settings. Second, it maintains robust parsing performance as document length increases. Through end-to-end modeling with SR-SWA, Unlimited OCR 2 filters redundant visual tokens while preserving relevant cross-page information, achieving the highest Overall scores and state-of-the-art performance on both cross-page text and table metrics, T-Text and T-Table, respectively, from dozens of pages on MPDocBench to hundreds of pages on MarathonDocBench. Third, it establishes a new state-of-the-art in long-document parsing, outperforming leading closed-source models and top-tier open-source MLLMs across these benchmarks. Furthermore, Unlimited OCR 2 retains strong single-page recognition capabilities, achieving an Overall score of 94.02% on OmniDocBench in Table <a href="#S5.T3" title="Table 3 ‣ 5.1 Benchmarks and Metrics ‣ 5 Evaluation ‣ Unlimited OCR Works 2Pioneering the OCR-3.0 Era: From Long- to Unlimited-Horizon Parsing" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">3</span></a>, confirming that its sparse attention design preserves fine-grained local recognition.</p>
</div>
<figure id="S5.T4" class="ltx_table">
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering" style="font-size:80%;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_table"><span id="S5.T4.7" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:113%;">Table 4</span>: </span><span id="S5.T4.8" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:113%;">Feasibility evaluation of the Unlimited-Horizon Decoding Paradigm. Sequential chunk processing reduces peak KV cache memory at <math id="S5.T4.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="B=1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>B</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">B=1</annotation></semantics></math> and improves end-to-end throughput at <math id="S5.T4.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="B=16" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>B</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>16</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">B=16</annotation></semantics></math>, enabling hundred-page parsing under constrained GPU memory.</span></figcaption>
<table id="S5.T4.9" class="ltx_tabular ltx_centering ltx_align_middle">
<tr id="S5.T4.9.1" class="ltx_tr">

<td id="S5.T4.9.1.3" class="ltx_td ltx_align_center ltx_border_tt" style="padding:0.85pt 8.0pt;"><span id="S5.T4.9.1.3.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold" style="font-size:80%;">TPS (<math id="S5.T4.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="B=16" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>B</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>16</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">B=16</annotation></semantics></math>)</span></td></tr>

<td id="S5.T4.9.2.3" class="ltx_td ltx_align_center ltx_border_t" style="padding:0.85pt 8.0pt;"><span id="S5.T4.9.2.3.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:80%;">360</span></td></tr>

</table>
</figure>
</section>
<section id="S5.SS3" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">5.3 </span>Scaling with Document Length</h3>

<section id="S5.SS3.SSS1" class="ltx_subsubsection">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsubsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsubsection">5.3.1 </span>Feasibility of Unlimited-horizon Parsing</h4>

<div id="S5.SS3.SSS1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S5.SS3.SSS1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Benefiting from SR-SWA and the Unlimited-Horizon Decoding Paradigm, Unlimited OCR 2 enables efficient parsing of extremely long documents under constrained GPU memory. We evaluate its feasibility on the hundred-page MarathonDocBench benchmark by measuring peak KV cache memory and end-to-end throughput, as reported in Table <a href="#S5.T4" title="Table 4 ‣ 5.2 Main Results ‣ 5 Evaluation ‣ Unlimited OCR Works 2Pioneering the OCR-3.0 Era: From Long- to Unlimited-Horizon Parsing" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">4</span></a>. Compared with standard decoding, page-level chunking with boundary-page KV cache reuse reduces peak KV cache memory from 47.00 GB to 1.77 GB under single-sequence inference (<math id="S5.SS3.SSS1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="B=1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>B</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">B=1</annotation></semantics></math>). Meanwhile, end-to-end throughput increases from 360 to 1,315 TPS under concurrent inference with <math id="S5.SS3.SSS1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="B=16" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>B</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>16</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">B=16</annotation></semantics></math>. These results demonstrate that sequential chunk processing with KV cache reuse substantially reduces memory requirements while improving throughput, making hundred-page document parsing more practical under limited GPU memory.</p>
</div>
<figure id="S5.F6" class="ltx_figure"><object type="image/svg+xml" data="2610.39308v2/latency_length_combined.svg" id="S5.F6.g1" class="ltx_graphics ltx_centering ltx_img_landscape" style="aspect-ratio:476/185;" width="476" height="185"></object>
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure"><span id="S5.F6.3" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Figure 6</span>: </span><span id="S5.F6.4" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:90%;">Performance and efficiency comparison across varying document lengths. Unlimited-OCR 2 demonstrates (a) robust parsing accuracy and (b) near-constant decoding latency (ms/step) as document length scaling.</span></figcaption>
</figure>
</section>
<section id="S5.SS3.SSS2" class="ltx_subsubsection">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsubsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsubsection">5.3.2 </span>Length-Invariant Accuracy</h4>

<div id="S5.SS3.SSS2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S5.SS3.SSS2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">To verify whether extending the document horizon compromises parsing fidelity, we evaluate the performance trajectories of Unlimited OCR 2 across continuously increasing document lengths. As illustrated in Figure <a href="#S5.F6" title="Figure 6 ‣ 5.3.1 Feasibility of Unlimited-horizon Parsing ‣ 5.3 Scaling with Document Length ‣ 5 Evaluation ‣ Unlimited OCR Works 2Pioneering the OCR-3.0 Era: From Long- to Unlimited-Horizon Parsing" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">6</span></a> (a), frontier Vision-Language Models (VLMs) typically experience a noticeable performance degradation as the sequence length grows, primarily caused by attention diffusion and context dilution over ultra-long horizons. In contrast, Unlimited OCR 2 exhibits remarkable length-invariant accuracy. By leveraging SR-SWA to dynamically isolate and retrieve only the most relevant visual tokens, our model maintains consistently high parsing precision from short sequences up to extreme horizons of 300 pages.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S5.SS3.SSS3" class="ltx_subsubsection">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsubsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsubsection">5.3.3 </span>Constant Per-Step Decoding Latency</h4>

<div id="S5.SS3.SSS3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S5.SS3.SSS3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Figure <a href="#S5.F6" title="Figure 6 ‣ 5.3.1 Feasibility of Unlimited-horizon Parsing ‣ 5.3 Scaling with Document Length ‣ 5 Evaluation ‣ Unlimited OCR Works 2Pioneering the OCR-3.0 Era: From Long- to Unlimited-Horizon Parsing" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">6</span></a> (b) examines how decoding efficiency scales with document length. All measurements are conducted in Gundam mode with a batch size of 3 and a fixed generation length of 1,024 tokens per page. As the document length grows, Full Attention incurs rapidly growing per-step decoding latency because each query must attend to a linearly expanding visual context. While R-SWA mitigates this overhead by bounding local window, its remote visual scope still scales with sequence length, leading to noticeable latency accumulation over ultra-long horizons. In contrast, SR-SWA strictly bounds the effective per-query attention scope, achieving near-constant per-step decoding latency from short contexts up to hundred-page documents. Consequently, its latency and throughput advantage over Full Attention and naive windowed baselines becomes increasingly pronounced as document length scales, confirming the computational viability of our paradigm for real-world long-document parsing.</p>
</div>
</section>
</section>
</section>
<section id="S6" class="ltx_section">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_section"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_section">6 </span>Limitation and Future Work</h2>

<div id="S6.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S6.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Although Unlimited OCR 2 enables efficient parsing of hundred-page documents, its training data remains limited in diversity, and further data refinement will improve its robustness and generalization. More importantly, the current sparse-attention mechanism does not preserve global document information, limiting its understanding of document-level structures such as heading hierarchies. Future work may introduce architectures such as linear attention to retain global information with constant per-token computational cost, further improving document-level structure understanding.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S7" class="ltx_section">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_section"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_section">7 </span>Conclusion</h2>

<div id="S7.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S7.p1.1" class="ltx_p">In this technical report, we presented Unlimited OCR 2, a next-generation architecture tailored for unlimited-horizon document parsing. Specifically, Unlimited OCR 2 introduces Sparse Reference Sliding Window Attention (SR-SWA) to break the long-context visual computation bottleneck, guaranteeing constant per-token computational complexity throughout decoding. Additionally, integrated with an optimized page-split decoding paradigm, the model significantly mitigates GPU memory consumption, enabling robust unlimited-horizon inference on resource-constrained hardware. Extensive evaluations and analysis confirm that Unlimited OCR 2 maintains superior parsing accuracy alongside exceptional efficiency across all scales, thereby pioneering the OCR-3.0 era of unlimited-horizon document understanding.</p>
</div>
</section>
